title: SLI orchestration bridge and error-budget mapper
creator: Elena Rodriguez
description: Build an SLI orchestration layer and mapping tool that ties per-service SLIs to initiative-level error budgets and OKR metrics. This ticket covers product requirements, UX wireframes for the OKR -> SLI mapping UI, the backend mapping schema for per-route SLIs and budget allocations, and a rollforward scheduler that proposes throttles/rollbacks when projected burn exceeds thresholds. Goal: make reliability commitments traceable from executive OKRs down to individual routes and rollout policies.
acceptance_criteria: UI: A new 'Reliability Bridge' tab in the Console where PMs can create mapping rules that link OKRs to one or more SLIs and set allocation weights for error budgets.
Backend: Schema and API to store mapping rules (service -> SLI -> OKR key -> weight) and computed allocation snapshots.
Automation: A scheduled job that computes projected error-budget burn over 7/30/90-day horizons and flags mappings with >80% projected burn for review.
Rollforward scheduler: UI action that suggests 'pause rollout', 'reduce concurrency', or 'fallback model' with one-click apply to Dedicated/Hosted routing policies.
Telemetry: Dashboard panel that shows per-mapping SLI trends, allocated vs actual error budget, and links to the associated runbooks and incidents.
Docs: Confluence spec + runbook describing mapping semantics, weight interpretation, and owner responsibilities.
implementation_notes: Mapping model: store weights as floats (0-1) with normalization per-OKR; allow manual override and an 'auto-normalize' option.
SLI types supported in initial rollout: latency_p95, availability_success_rate, model-error-rate (application-level), and embedding-failure-rate.
Compute job will depend on SLI rollups already emitted to telemetry topics (dataplane -> telemetry pipeline). We'll consume the existing SLI_v2 topic.
Rollforward actions are implemented as a change in routing policy CR (canary.throttle/concurrency_limit) and must create an audit log entry and post a comment in the mapping object.
Data retention for mapping snapshots: 90 days to support retros and root-cause analysis.
decisions: Prioritize service-level mapping first; route-level granularities will be added in Q3 2026.
Use a weight-based allocation model to allow fractional sharing of an OKR's error budget across multiple SLIs.
Rollforward actions will be implemented as idempotent routing policy updates with an audit webhook to the runbook channel.
risks: Incorrect weight normalization could under/over-allocate budgets and give misleading projections.
Automated rollforward actions have blast radius — must require two-step confirmation for production-runbooks.
Telemetry lag could make projected burn unreliable; we need to surface data freshness prominently.
Cross-team coordination: legal/compliance signoff may be required for private deployments that adjust routing.
